subject: Game Theory
title: Information Asymmetry in Bargaining
description: A micro-lesson that makes Information Asymmetry in Bargaining usable.

hook.text: You're selling a car. You know it needs a new transmission. The buyer doesn't. Who has the advantage?

buildup.text: In bargaining, private information creates power. Knowing more than the other side lets you manipulate terms.

discovery.text: But information advantages can backfire: buyers who suspect hidden flaws may walk away entirely.

twist.text: The 'market for lemons' problem: if buyers can't trust quality, only bad products get sold.

climax.text: Warranties, inspections, and disclosures evolved as solutions to information asymmetry in deals.

punchline.text: Hidden info helps short-term, hurts long-term.

quiz.question: What is the 'market for lemons' problem?
options: Buyers can't assess quality, so good products leave the market
